Suggestion.description:
A concept offered to the user in the suggest UI, with label, description, group, and current selection state.

Returned in `SuggestResult.suggestions`. `selected: true` means the concept is already in the current marking; clicking it again removes it. `order` controls display position within the group. `views` carries all render-format representations so the UI can switch formats without a second query. `source` distinguishes concepts from parsing the input (`'parse'`), preset shortcuts (`'preset'`), or alias matches (`'alias'`).

categoryId.description: The category the concept belongs to.

conceptId.description: The id of the suggested concept.

description.description: Secondary label (longer name or alternate view).

gated.description: True when this concept matches the active filter but is currently gated by the scheme's rules (a rule prerequisite is unmet, or a constraint forbids it). Gated suggestions are surfaced as non-selectable, explanatory rows so the user can see why the concept is unavailable. Only populated when the caller passes `includeGated: true` and a filter is active.

label.description: Primary display label in the current render format.

requires.description: When `gated` is true, the unmet prerequisite concept ids that would unlock this concept. Empty array when the concept is gated by a constraint with no specific prerequisite (e.g. mutual exclusion).

requiresDisplay.description: Resolved operational display (rendered marking view) for each id in `requires`, index-aligned, so the unlock row can read "add X first" with the marking rather than the raw id. `requires` stays as the machine keys.

selected.description: True if this concept is already in the current marking.

source.description: `preset` on a row that offers a label preset, whose `conceptId` is `preset:` followed by the preset id. A concept row leaves it unset.

Warning.description:
A non-blocking informational signal surfaced in a result's `warnings`.

Unlike `ValidationError`, warnings never affect `valid`. `kind: 'deprecation'` fires when a deprecated concept is asserted, and `replacement` names a suggested successor concept. `kind: 'rule'` fires when a scheme's authored `warn` rule matches the marking, with the rule's id as `ruleId`. `kind: 'notice'` is the engine speaking about the operation itself rather than about anything the scheme declares; its `ruleId`, when present, is an engine-reserved id beginning with `_`, the same convention a `ValidationError` follows.

A marking's warnings come in a fixed order: deprecations first, then the scheme's rule warnings in the order the scheme declares its rules, then the engine's notices. An aggregate's warnings are about the rolled-up marking, not about each marking that fed it.

categoryId.description: Category this warning relates to (when applicable)

conceptId.description: Concept this warning relates to (when applicable). A rule warning names one when the rule's `when` names exactly one concept the marking holds.

conceptName.description: Resolved operational display for `conceptId` (the concept's rendered marking view), for a consumer that shows the warning next to the concept. `conceptId` stays as the machine key; this is the human-visible string.

kind.description: Warning kind: 'deprecation' for a deprecated concept, 'rule' for a scheme's authored `warn` rule, 'notice' for the engine's own notice.

replacement.description: When kind=deprecation, the suggested replacement concept id (if any)

replacementName.description: When kind=deprecation, the resolved operational display for `replacement` (the successor concept's rendered marking view). `replacement` stays as the machine key; this is the human-visible string.

ruleId.description: The scheme rule that gave a `rule` warning, or the engine-reserved id of a `notice`. Absent on a deprecation warning.

WarningKind.description: Non-blocking warning category: a deprecated concept, a scheme's authored `warn` rule, or a notice the engine gives about the operation itself.

description:
What suggest answers: the concepts a picker may offer, and nothing about the marking itself.

How the current marking reads and whether it stands are what validate and process answer, and suggest does not repeat them. A caller that wants both in one round trip asks process for them with `suggestFor`.

suggestions.description: The concepts on offer, in display order.

warnings.description: Advisories raised while building the options, such as a concept source that could not answer in full. Empty when there were none. Advisories about the marking itself belong to validate and process.
